title: feat: split Quest vs Paid spending by community models
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Start every linear time-series y-axis at 0 across the five observability dashboards (21 panels), with a test that fails if a new panel doesn't. The balance panels keep their soft minimum so negative balances stay visible; the log-scale concentration panel is unchanged.
- Split Users & Balances "Quest vs Paid spending" into Paid/Quest × Pollinations/community models. Totals are unchanged: community spending was already included but not visible. Over the last 90 days it was 2.8% of Paid and 18.6% of Quest, and the 07/11 spike is Quest Pollen spent on one community model.
- Fix panel descriptions that called Paid consumption revenue. 75% of community-model spend and all BYOP markup are credited back to owners in the payer's bucket, so Paid consumption isn't cash or Pollinations revenue.

Checked with `npm test`, the new query against production Tinybird, and the panel rendered in a local Grafana.

gist.headline: The ledger grows branches
gist.blurb: The observability garden now separates Paid and Quest spending by Pollinations and community models. The totals were always there; now the paths through the pollen are visible too.
gist.summary: Updated 21 observability dashboard panels so linear time-series axes begin at zero, and split the Users & Balances Quest vs Paid spending view into Paid/Quest × Pollinations/community-model series while preserving totals.
gist.impact: Operators can now clearly identify community-model spending—including the 07/11 Quest spike—while dashboard descriptions accurately distinguish consumption from revenue and new panels are tested for zero-based axes.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy accounting garden: Polli, wearing tiny accountant glasses, tends four labeled flowering branches representing Paid and Quest spending across Pollinations and community models. A friendly CRT monitor robot displays a zero-based chart with a visible community-model bloom, while vines and code-plants make the dashboard work feel like careful garden bookkeeping.
